entities.summary:
Carlo d'Aragona Tagliavia, 1st Prince of Castelvetrano, was a Sicilian-Spanish nobleman and viceroy who played a pivotal role in the politics of the Spanish Empire in the late 16th century.

Born into a family of Italian nobility, Tagliavia was educated in the arts of war and administration, and served as a military commander in the Spanish army. In 1585, he was appointed as the viceroy of Sicily, a position he held until his death in 1599.

During his tenure, Tagliavia oversaw the suppression of a rebellion led by the Sicilian Vespers, a popular uprising against Spanish rule. He also implemented various reforms aimed at strengthening the Spanish Empire's grip on the island.

Despite his efforts, Tagliavia's legacy was marked by controversy. His actions as viceroy were often seen as heavy-handed, and his policies towards the local population were criticized by some historians as oppressive.

In the centuries following his death, Tagliavia's reputation has undergone a reevaluation, with some historians viewing him as a key figure in the development of the Spanish Empire's administrative structures in the Mediterranean.

'When I die, I will be remembered as a just and fair ruler, beloved by my people.' - Carlo d'Aragona Tagliavia
